The theorem's slope is (e(x,t0+h)-e(x,t0))/h also when h<0, because reversing both differences changes neither quotient. Thus its absolute value is at most B. If x∉Q, N002 makes both densities zero and gives the same estimate with right side zero. Discharge L1 and quantify x,h: for all x and all 0<|h|<η, |(e(x,t0+h)-e(x,t0))/h|≤B 1_Q(x). The sequential criterion for limits in R now gives the full two-sided difference-quotient limit at zero. Together with F002 and the definition of E this proves the complete conclusion with coefficient one on both squared norms and without any time-zero assertion.
